answer.description:
Free-form answer for `breakpointType: "question"` asks (the `ask_user`
tool): an option id/string or arbitrary JSON. Ignored for plain
allow/deny approvals.

rule.description:
Rule payload for `remember`; when absent the server derives one from
the tool call (same shape as `ToolApprovalRequired.suggestedRule`).

rememberedRule.description: The persisted rule when the resolve carried `remember` (P1.6).

ArtifactDetailRecord.description: Artifact metadata plus extracted text and version chain.

BudgetStatusRecord.description: Live budget picture: config, window spend and derived status.

ComparisonDeltasRecord.description: Metric deltas between two runs (always `right - left`).

ConversationApprovalsParams.description: Approval audit rows for one conversation.

ConversationMessagesParams.description: Paginated transcript read for one legacy conversation.

ConversationSearchParams.description: Full-text search over conversation message content.

ConversationUpdateParams.description: Patch a conversation; `None` fields are left unchanged.

DeletedResult.description: Result of a delete-style mutation: the removed record id.

DirectoryListingRecord.description: Sub-directories of a path for the folder browser.

EmptyParams.description: Parameters that carry no fields of their own.

ExtensionDiagnosticRecord.description: One diagnostic emitted while loading an installed plugin.

ExtensionStatusResult.description:
Read-only snapshot of the extension admin surface: installed plugins,
supervised workers, hook review state, discovered skills, plugin-bundled MCP
servers and the MCP tool policy.

GitInfoRecord.description: Current git branch of a directory.

compactUpToCursor.description: Set only on a `role: "summary"` item: the `session.compacted` cutoff.

cursor.description:
Durable cursor of the item's own event (the `rust_events.rowid`), stable
for the lifetime of the store. Clients can use it as a render key.

model.description: Model that produced the assistant item, when the run recorded one.

occurredAt.description: RFC3339 timestamp of the item's event.

runId.description: Durable run the item belongs to.

usage.description:
Cumulative usage reported by the model call that produced the assistant
item (absent for user/tool items and imported history).

HookRecord.description:
One hook declaration from an enabled plugin plus its review state. `approved`
is true only when the stored review hash matches the hook's exact trust hash,
so changing the command/args/env/matcher resets approval.

HookReviewParams.description:
Approve or reject one hook declaration. `trust_hash` must equal the hook's
current trust hash, so an operator cannot approve a definition they did not
review; a mismatch fails closed.

IdempotentIdParams.description: Address one numeric legacy record for a mutation.

IdempotentParams.description: A mutation without a target record (for example clearing an override).

McpAddServerParams.description: Add a global MCP server configuration.

McpServerAdminRecord.description:
One configured MCP server with its live status and discovered tools.
`env`/`headers`/`cwd` are deliberately absent (they can carry credentials).

McpServerNameParams.description: Address one configured MCP server by name.

McpServerRecord.description: One MCP server bundled by an enabled plugin.

McpStoreInstallParams.description: Install an MCP server from the official registry by registry name.

McpStoreItemRecord.description: One server returned by an MCP registry search.

McpStoreSearchResult.description: Registry search result plus the query that produced it.

McpToolListResult.description: All tools discovered across connected servers.

McpToolPolicyRecord.description:
The configured MCP tool policy. `enabled` is `None` when the policy keeps
every non-disabled tool; `disabled` always applies.

McpToolRecord.description: One tool exposed by a configured MCP server.

McpUpdateServerParams.description: Partial update for a global MCP server configuration.

MemoryExtractParams.description: Run LLM memory extraction over one conversation.

MemoryExtractResult.description:
Outcome of `memory.extract`. Mirrors Python `ExtractResponse`: `status` is
`error` / `skipped` / `completed`; `detail` carries the skip reason or the
error message; `stored_count` is the number of persisted candidates.

MemoryScoreBreakdown.description: Score breakdown of why a memory is retained.

MemoryStatsRecord.description: Dashboard counters for the memory subsystem.

ModelInfoRecord.description: One model advertised by a provider row's cached catalog.

ParseCronResult.description: Parsed cron schedule plus the next fire times.

steps.description:
Full step list with statuses, so a client can render pending steps that
never emit their own `plan.step_*` event.

storePlanId.description:
Durable `plans.id` the runtime persisted for this model plan, when the
run's session is bound to a legacy conversation. Clients use it to
approve/execute the plan through the App Protocol; `None` when the
session is not conversation-bound.

PlanExecuteResult.description:
Result of starting a plan execution: the durable plan and the run that
carries its canonical `plan.*` events.

PlanUpdateParams.description: Edit a draft plan's title and/or steps.

PluginEnabledParams.description:
Enable or disable one installed plugin. Disabling never loads the tree;
enabling re-verifies the content hash and fails closed on a tampered tree.

PluginRecord.description: One installed plugin as seen by the admin surface.

contentVerified.description:
True only when the on-disk tree still matches the recorded content hash
*and* its manifest identity. An enabled plugin with
`contentVerified: false` is treated as failed by the runtime (its hooks,
skills and MCP servers are not loaded) even though the install record
remains visible for diagnosis.

runId.description: Session rules attach to a live run; required when `scope = "session"`.

PolicyRuleRecord.description:
Wire mirror of `cool_security::PolicyRule` — kept as plain strings so the
protocol crate carries no cool-security dependency.

tool.description: Tool name, or `"*"` for every tool.

runId.description: Session rules of this run when `scope = "session"`.

scope.description: Optional scope filter (`session|project|user`); absent lists all.

ProviderRecord.description: One provider row. The encrypted API key is intentionally absent.

apiKeyHint.description:
Masked hint for the stored API key (`abc…wxyz`), or `None` when no key is
set. Never the key itself; mirrors the Python `ProviderOut.api_key_hint`.

ProvidersPreviewModelsParams.description:
Live model-list probe for an unsaved provider (create form). The plaintext
key is used in memory only and never persisted.

RecentDirectoriesRecord.description: Recently used working directories and the global default.

ReplayParams.description: Prepare a replay run from an existing run with optional overrides.

ReplayResult.description: Result of preparing a replay run.

ResearchCancelResult.description: Result of cancelling a research run.

runtimeRunId.description:
Canonical run id that streams this run's `research.*` events (set on
`research.create`/`research.rerun` responses; not part of the row).

confidence.description:
Python stores confidence as a label (`high`/`medium`/`low`), not a
numeric score.

RssFetchResult.description:
Outcome of a forced feed fetch: how many novel entries were stored.
A fetch/parse failure is recorded on the subscription and reported as
`new_entries: 0` (Python `fetch_feed` never raises to the caller).

RunListParams.description: List runs of a conversation, newest first.

RunSubscribeParams.description:
Subscribes the calling connection to another connection's run so live
`run.event` notifications fan out to every subscriber, not only the
connection that started the run.

lastSeq.description: Durable cursor to catch up from; live events continue with `seq > last_seq`.

terminal.description: True when the run is already terminal; no live events will follow.

compactUpToCursor.description:
Cursor of the newest compacted history item. Items with a cursor `<=`
this value are covered by `summary`.

summary.description:
Rolling summary text, when the compaction produced one. `session.history`
projects it as a summary item so the chat can render the compacted block.

importedEvents.description: Canonical history events projected from the legacy transcript.

truncated.description:
True when the projection is not the complete legacy transcript: the
bound was reached and/or leading orphan tool rows were dropped. Older
messages stay readable through `conversations.messages`.

SessionForConversationParams.description:
Binds one legacy conversation to a durable Rust session, importing the
legacy transcript once so chat turns run on the canonical event model.

beforeCursor.description:
Exclusive, opaque durable cursor: only history derived from events
appended before `before_cursor` is returned. Older pages pass the
`next_cursor` of the previous page; absent, the newest page is returned.

nextCursor.description:
Exclusive cursor for the next older page, or `None` when this page is
the oldest. Pass it as `beforeCursor` to continue paging.

longTaskMode.description:
Long-running task mode: the run is marked `long_task` and the existing
task progress file (`.cool/task/progress.md`, maintained by the bundled
long-running-task skill) is injected into the system prompt so the
agent resumes from tracked state. Ignored in planning mode.

planMode.description:
Planning mode: the runtime owns the system prompt (a canonical planning
directive) and marks the run mode as `plan`, so the model produces a
plan through the trusted `update_plan` tool instead of executing.

systemPrompt.description:
Caller-supplied system prompt. Ignored in planning mode, where the
runtime owns the system prompt so a caller cannot steer the plan.

SessionRunsParams.description: List durable runs of one session, newest first.

SkillAdminRecord.description: One skill in the global skills store.

source.description: Where the skill was loaded from (`user` for the Rust store).

SkillCreateParams.description: Create a new skill (`SKILL.md`) in the global store.

scope.description:
Accepted for parity with the Python API (`global`/`user`); the Rust store
is a single directory and reports `user`.

SkillDeleteParams.description: Delete a skill from the global store by name.

SkillListParams.description: List skills, optionally filtered by source.

SkillListResult.description: All skills in the global store.

SkillRecord.description: One skill parsed from an enabled plugin's `SKILL.md` tree.

parentRunId.description:
Durable parent run the delegation belongs to, when the caller is an
agent-initiated `spawn_subagent` tool call.

SubagentRunCancelResult.description: Result of cancelling a subagent run.

SubagentRunDetailRecord.description: Subagent run plus its isolated transcript.

SystemPromptRecord.description:
The effective default system prompt and where it comes from. `source` is
`inline` when an operator-set prompt is stored, otherwise `builtin` (Rust
ships no bundled prompt file, so an unset default is empty and no system
message is sent).

SystemPromptSetParams.description:
Set the default system prompt. An empty (or whitespace-only) prompt clears it
and resets the effective state to the built-in default.

template.description:
Built-in workflow template slug. When set, the server fills the prompt,
cron schedule, workflow type, tool whitelist and delivery channels from
the matching [`TaskTemplateRecord`] unless the caller supplied them.

scheduleDescription.description:
Derived server-side (like the Python `TaskOut`): human-readable schedule
text and upcoming fire times for a valid cron schedule.

TaskRunDetailRecord.description: Task run plus the transcript of its isolated conversation.

TaskTemplateRecord.description:
A built-in recurring-workflow preset surfaced by `tasks.templates` so the UI
can prefill the create form.

TimelineRecord.description: Inspector timeline for a run, rebuilt from the append-only event log.

matchedRule.description:
The exec/policy rule that produced this ask (`None` when the ask came
from the capability fallback).

suggestedRule.description:
A rule the client can persist via `approval.resolve {remember}` to
stop prompting for equivalent calls.

ToolCatalogRecord.description:
One tool registered in the running Rust agent runtime, as shown by the
agent-constructor and subagent tool pickers. `dangerous` marks a tool whose
default decision is `Ask` (requires approval); macro-backed tools are
flagged via the `macro_` name prefix.

WebhookEndpointRecord.description: One webhook endpoint row. The HMAC `secret` is intentionally absent.

WorkerRecord.description: One compatibility worker supervised by the extension runtime.
